questions.question: _____ is the science and art of cultivating fruits, vegetables, flowers and ornamental plants.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Horticulture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Horticulture is derived from the **Latin words “hortus” (garden) and “cultura” (cultivation)**, meaning garden cultivation.
 
• It covers multiple categories, including **pomology, olericulture, floriculture, landscape horticulture, and post-harvest management**.

questions.question: In 2023, Government of India has proposed to launch the ‘Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana’ ___________ to skill lakhs of youth within the next three years covering new age courses like coding, AI, robotics, mechatronics, IOT, 3D printing, drones and soft skills.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 2023, the Government of India launched ‘Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana** 4.0** (PMKVY 4.0)’, as part of its continued effort to upskill India's youth in emerging technologies.
 
• The aim is to train over** 4.2 lakh youth **over the next three years, covering modern areas like artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, coding, drones, 3D printing, mechatronics, Internet of Things (IoT), and soft skills.
 
• The scheme also focuses on industry-based learning to ensure that participants acquire skills that align with market demands.
 
• The **key objectives** include:
 
 
• Enhancing employability by providing vocational training and certification in new-age technologies.
 
• Incorporating international standards into the curriculum for globally recognized certifications.
 
• Promoting self-employment and entrepreneurship alongside providing placements in relevant industries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) has been implemented in phases since its inception, each aiming to build on the last in terms of training India’s workforce for new and emerging industries.

 
• **PMKVY 1.0 (2015-2016):**

 
 
• Launch Date: 15 July **2015**
 
• Goal: To provide skill training to around 24 lakh youth across the country in various sectors.
 
• Focused on short-term training programs through training centers accredited by the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC).
 
• Outcome: More than 19 lakh candidates were trained, but the placement rate was a key challenge, as the training did not always align with industry demand.
 
 
 
• **PMKVY 2.0 (2016-2020):**
 
 
• Launch Date: 2 October **2016**
 
• Goal: Upskilling of over 1 crore people by 2020.
 
• Expanded to cover more sectors and introduced Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) for workers who already possess certain skills.
 
• Focus on placements with the introduction of mandatory placement tracking and support.
 
• Increased participation of state governments in the scheme for local adaptability.
 
• Special Projects were introduced to cater to the specific needs of certain industries, job roles, or regions.
 
• Outcome: It significantly increased reach but faced criticism for not achieving a high placement rate despite the broader scope.
 
 
 
• **PMKVY 3.0 (2020-2021):**
 
• Launch Date: January 15, **2021**
 
 
• Goal: To skill over 8 lakh people in emerging areas over one year.
 
• Shifted focus towards local demand-based skill training.
 
• Emphasized digital learning to adapt to the post-pandemic world, incorporating online and blended training modes.
 
• Introduction of district skill committees to identify demand-driven skills specific to local areas.
 
• Strengthened the focus on apprenticeship training and linking skilling with employment.
 
• Outcome: PMKVY 3.0 aimed to refine earlier challenges by localizing skill development and incorporating emerging technologies like AI, cybersecurity, and cloud computing.
 
 

Each version of the PMKVY scheme aimed to improve India’s skill ecosystem by adapting to the evolving needs of the labor market and technological advancements. PMKVY 4.0 continues this effort by focusing on futuristic technologies and aligning the training program with global standards.

⇒ 36 + k ≡ 0 (mod 9)

⇒ k ≡ -36 (mod 9)

⇒ k ≡ 0 (mod 9)

Since we need the smallest non-zero value of k:

k = 9

**The smallest non-zero value of k so that 48397k5 is divisible by 9 is 9.**

**Given:**

Speed for two-fifth of the distance = 40 km/h.

Speed for the remaining distance = 60 km/h.

**Formula Used:**

Average speed = Total distance travelled / Total time

**Calculation:**

Let the total distance be d km.

Distance traveled at 40 km/h = (2/5)d km.

Distance traveled at 60 km/h = (3/5)d km.

Time taken to travel (2/5)d km at 40 km/h = (2/5)d / 40

Time taken to travel (3/5)d km at 60 km/h = (3/5)d / 60

Total Distance = d km

Total Time = (2/5)d / 40 + (3/5)d / 60

Total Time = (2d / 200) + (3d / 300)

Total Time = d(1/100 + 1/100)

Total Time = d(2/100)

Total Time = d / 50

Average Speed = d / (d / 50)

Average Speed = d × 50 / d

questions.question: Half the perimeter of a rectangular garden, whose length is 8 cm more than its width, is 42 cm. Find the area of the rectangular garden.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Half the perimeter of a rectangular garden = 42 cm

Length = Width + 8 cm

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (Length + Width)

Area of a rectangle = Length × Width

**Calculation:**

Let the width be W cm.

Then the length is W + 8 cm.

Half the perimeter = 42 cm

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × 42 = 84 cm

⇒ 2 × (Length + Width) = 84

⇒ Length + Width = 42

⇒ (W + 8) + W = 42

⇒ 2W + 8 = 42

⇒ 2W = 42 - 8

⇒ 2W = 34

⇒ W = 34 / 2

⇒ W = 17 cm

Length = W + 8 = 17 + 8 = 25 cm

Area = Length × Width

⇒ Area = 25 cm × 17 cm

⇒ Area = 425 cm²

**The area of the rectangular garden is 425 cm².**

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work separately in 10 days and 8 days, respectively. If they work alternately and A begins the work, in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(10, 8) = 40 units.

Efficiency of A = 40 ÷ 10 = 4 units/day, Efficiency of B = 40 ÷ 8 = 5 units/day.

In 2 days, working alternately (A starts), work done = 4 + 5 = 9 units.

In 4 cycles (8 days), work done = 9 × 4 = 36 units.

Remaining work = 40 − 36 = 4 units. On the 9th day, A completes 4 units in 1 day.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 10 days

Time taken by B = 8 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of given days

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done on the 1st day by A = 4 units

⇒ Work done on the 2ⁿd day by B = 5 units

⇒ Total work done in 2 days (1 cycle) = 4 + 5 = 9 units

⇒ Number of complete cycles before total work is reached = 40 ÷ 9 = 4 cycles (with a remainder)

⇒ Work done in 4 cycles (8 days) = 4 × 9 = 36 units

⇒ Remaining work = 40 − 36 = 4 units

⇒ The 9th day begins a new cycle, so it is A's turn to work.

⇒ Time taken by A to complete the remaining work = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of A = 4 ÷ 4 = 1 day

Alternate Day Work

When individuals work on alternate days, group their work into cycles. Multiply the cycle work to get as close to the total work as possible, then allocate the remaining work sequentially to the person whose turn it is.

Pipes & Cisterns

The approach is identical to Time and Work problems. The only difference is that an outlet or emptying pipe is assigned a negative efficiency.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each individual. If they work together for the same duration, wages are directly distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

questions.question: If P sin 60° = Q cosec 45°, then the value of (P²+Q²)/(P²-Q²) is equal to:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

From the given equation: P/Q = cosec 45° ÷ sin 60° = √2 ÷ (√3/2) = 2√2/√3

Squaring both sides gives: P²/Q² = 8/3

Applying the Componendo and Dividendo rule directly:

(P² + Q²) / (P² − Q²) = (8 + 3) / (8 − 3) = 11/5

**∴ The correct answer is 11/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

P sin 60° = Q cosec 45°

**Concept Used:**

Standard trigonometric values: sin 60° = √3/2 and cosec 45° = √2

**Calculations:**

⇒ P × (√3/2) = Q × √2

⇒ P/Q = √2 ÷ (√3/2)

⇒ P/Q = (2√2) / √3

Squaring both sides of the equation:

⇒ P²/Q² = (2√2)² / (√3)²

⇒ P²/Q² = 8/3

Let P² = 8k and Q² = 3k. Substituting these into the required expression:

⇒ (P² + Q²) / (P² − Q²)

⇒ (8k + 3k) / (8k − 3k)

⇒ 11k / 5k

⇒ 11/5

**∴ The correct answer is 11/5.**

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

If a/b = c/d, then (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d). This property is highly useful for simplifying algebraic equations and expressions involving the sum and difference of terms.

Standard Trigonometric Ratios

It is essential to remember key angle values: sin 30° = 1/2, sin 45° = 1/√2, and sin 60° = √3/2. The cosecant function is the reciprocal of sine, meaning cosec θ = 1 / sin θ.

Basic Pythagorean Identities
